facts.text: I keep getting fevers that come and go.
I have painful sores (ulcers) on my legs.

facts.item: how long the fevers and leg sores have lasted
facts.text: The fevers and the leg sores have been going on for two months.
I have red, tender lumps on both of my legs.
About eight months ago I developed vertigo, a spinning feeling.
About eight months ago, at the same time as the vertigo, my left ear started to feel full.
A hearing test around the time of the vertigo, about eight months ago, showed I had nerve-type (sensorineural) hearing loss in my left ear.

facts.item: fever with chills in the past
facts.text: About two weeks after the ear symptoms started, I had a fever with chills.

facts.item: fever with chills in the past: response to treatment
facts.text: I got better with antibiotic tablets.
After the fever with chills, I noticed my gums had become enlarged.
At one point I got better after taking ibuprofen.
I take levothyroxine for my thyroid.
I've been caring for pets that were sick.

gold.reasoning: 1. Tuberculosis was considered but excluded because the IGRA was negative — “the test for latent tuberculosis by interferon gamma release assay (IGRA) was also negative.” 2. Brucellosis was considered but excluded by negative serology — “Serology for Brucella abortus and melitensis also came negative.” 3. Sarcoidosis was considered but made unlikely by a normal ACE level — “serum angiotensin converting enzyme level … was negative.”

notes: Index visit: the presentation with two months of recurrent fevers and painful leg ulcers (s001); s002–s007 are the history before it, s008–s017 the examination and workup, and s019–s021 later results of the same workup (given a time).

Earlier test results (audiometry, chest X-ray, ESR, sinus CT) are findings with a time; only the hearing loss, which audiometry 'confirmed', is also a patient fact. The patient is not assumed to know the chest X-ray or CT results.
The skin biopsy (x027) reports necrotising granulomatous vasculitis, which points to the diagnosis without naming it.
